outputs.exact_statement:
Let $G$ be any group, let $1\le m\le n$ be integers, and let $w_1,\ldots,w_m\in G*F_n$. If their exponent-sum matrix has row rank $m$ over $\mathbb Q$, then the canonical homomorphism $$G\longrightarrow
 (G*F_n)/\langle\!\langle w_1,\ldots,w_m\rangle\!\rangle$$ is injective. Equivalently, the system has a simultaneous solution in an overgroup of $G$.

Let $r\geq 0$ and $n\geq 1$, and let $k_1,\ldots,k_r$ be positive integers. For each $j\in\{1,\ldots,n\}$, let $\mathcal B_j$ be a finite ordered list of pairs $(i,s)$ with $1\leq i\leq r$ and $s\in\{1,-1\}$; repetitions are allowed. Set $$d_j=\sum_{(i,s)\in\mathcal B_j}k_i,
 \qquad
 b_{ij}=\sum_{\substack{(i',s)\in\mathcal B_j\\i'=i}}s,
 \qquad B=(b_{ij}).$$ Suppose that $B$ has row rank $r$ over $\mathbb Q$. For arbitrary $P_j\in\mathrm U(d_j)$, define $$D=\prod_{i=1}^r\mathrm U(k_i),
 \qquad
 F_j(X)=\operatorname{diag}_{(i,s)\in\mathcal B_j}(X_i^s)P_j
 \quad (X\in D).$$ Then there is $X\in D$ such that $$\label{eq:fixed-space-bound}
 \sum_{j=1}^n\dim_{\mathbb C}\ker(F_j(X)-I_{d_j})
 \ \geq\ \sum_{i=1}^r k_i.$$ Here $\mathrm U(0)$ and an empty product of groups are points, and the fixed-space dimension in dimension zero is zero.
For every group $G$, every positive integer $d$, and all unitaries $U,V\in M_d(\mathcal M)$, $$\ell(UV)\leq\ell(U)+\ell(V).$$

Let $w_1,\ldots,w_m\in G*F_n$ have exponent-sum matrix of row rank $m$ over $\mathbb Q$. Let $\Sigma$ be a connected oriented surface of genus zero obtained from a nonempty finite collection of signed word disks for these words by attaching bands that pair every slot exactly once, always with the same variable index and opposite traversal signs. If the words on all boundary components except possibly one are trivial in $G$, then every boundary word is trivial in $G$.

The finite statement also implies the version with arbitrary sets of variables and equations. Assume the exponent rows, each of finite support, are linearly independent over $\mathbb Q$. Any element of $G$ killed in the quotient has a normal-closure expression involving only finitely many relators and finitely many variables, including those in its conjugators. The corresponding finite exponent matrix still has independent rows, so Theorem 1 makes that element trivial.

If $A\ne1$, then $(A*\langle t\rangle)/\langle\!\langle w\rangle\!\rangle_H\ne1$ for every $w\in A*\langle t\rangle$.

Let $s_1,\ldots,s_n\in\{1,-1\}$ satisfy $\varepsilon:=\sum_i s_i\in\{1,-1\}$, let $k\geq1$ be an integer, and put $m=nk$. For every $P\in\mathop{\mathrm{U}}(m)$ there is an $X\in\mathop{\mathrm{U}}(k)$ such that $$F(X)=\operatorname{diag}(X^{s_1},\ldots,X^{s_n})P$$ fixes a complex subspace of dimension at least $k$.
